name: cron_field
summary: Parse a single cron field into its matching integer set
agent_instructions:
Implement a parser for a SINGLE cron field in a NEW file cron_field.py.

Provide a function with exactly this signature:
  match_field(field: str, lo: int, hi: int) -> set[int]

It expands one cron field over the inclusive range [lo, hi] and returns the set of matching integers. Supported syntax:
  - '*'            -> every value in [lo, hi]
  - a single int   -> {a}                       e.g. '5' -> {5}
  - 'a-b'          -> every value in [a, b]      e.g. '1-3' -> {1,2,3}
  - '*/s'          -> every s-th value from lo   e.g. lo=0,hi=10,'*/3' -> {0,3,6,9}
  - 'a-b/s'        -> every s-th value from a..b  e.g. '1-9/3' -> {1,4,7}
  - comma list     -> union of the above         e.g. '1,3,5-7' -> {1,3,5,6,7}

Validation (raise ValueError on ALL of these):
  1. A step <= 0 (e.g. '*/0', 'a-b/-1').
  2. A value or range endpoint outside [lo, hi].
  3. A reversed range where a > b (e.g. '5-1').
  4. Malformed tokens (empty token from a stray comma, non-integer, more than one '/').
  5. lo > hi passed by the caller.

Follow strict TDD: write pytest tests in test_cron_field.py covering every syntax form AND every ValueError case FIRST, confirm they fail, then implement. Return a real set[int].
